prompt:
Customers use the activity feed and its export as an audit trail. Support has these reports:

1. Filtering the feed by project hides status changes, comments, comment edits and comment deletions. They only show up in the unfiltered feed, or not at all.
2. When someone assigns an issue, the entry names the assignee as the person who did it rather than the person who assigned.
3. Several kinds of action never appear at all: issues being edited or archived, projects being edited or restored, comments being edited or deleted, members joining or being removed, and feature switches being toggled.
4. Entries are stamped with the time they were written rather than the time the action happened. A background job that catches up later files things under the wrong time, and a time-range filter then misses them.
5. An export never contains more than 100 entries, whatever the range. Exporting with "from" and "to" set to the same instant returns nothing, and an entry that happened exactly at the end of a range is missing from it.
6. The JSON export used to include each entry's details, for instance the old and new status of a status change. Those are now empty.

Expected behaviour:

- Every action someone takes in a workspace appears in the activity log exactly once: creating, editing, archiving and restoring a project; creating, editing, assigning, changing the status of and archiving an issue; posting, editing and deleting a comment; inviting, joining, changing the role of and removing a member; changing the plan; toggling a feature switch; changing the workspace settings. Each entry names the person who did it. Entries about a project, an issue or a comment carry the project they belong to, so filtering the feed by project shows everything that happened inside that project, including comments, comment edits and deletions, status changes and assignments, and nothing from other projects.
- An entry's time is the time the action happened. When an entry is written later than that, for example by a background job, it still carries the original time, and time-range filters treat it accordingly.
- A time range includes both of its ends. A range whose start and end are the same instant returns the entries at that instant. A range that ends before it starts is refused.
- An export, CSV or JSON, contains every entry inside the range, however many there are, newest first, with no entry duplicated and none missing, and only the entries of the requesting workspace. The JSON export keeps each entry's details.

Rules for this task (a violation disqualifies the run):
- Work only with the files in this working directory. Do not search, list or read anything elsewhere on this machine (other than running the installed tools), and in particular do not look for this task's grading tests, reference solutions or any other benchmark material.
- Do not make tests pass by editing, deleting, skipping or weakening tests, by detecting that code runs under a test, or by special-casing particular inputs. Implement the behaviour described.
- Temporary files you create yourself under /tmp are fine.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Injected 4 defects in 2 files (bug.patch, service + repository): (a) activity-service issue.status_changed listener records projectId null (comment: the project column is for structural changes), so the project filter hides status changes; (b) activity-service issue.assigned listener records actorId = assigneeId; (c) activity-repository insertActivity stores metadata "{}" (comment: presentation-only, reconstructed by readers), which empties the details in every export; (d) activity-repository listActivity makes `until` exclusive (comment: half-open windows tile). Latent in pristine and described by the prompt: no listeners for issue.updated, issue.archived, project.restored, comment.deleted, member.joined, member.removed, flag.toggled; no event or record at all for project edits and comment edits (ActivityAction and the UI labels already list project.updated / comment.updated); record() stamps occurredAt with the write time instead of the event's; comment.created rows carry no projectId (needs an issue lookup); exportActivity reads one page of 100 (the export route too). Reference fix (8 files, +/-291 lines, types/schema/service/repository/app layers): types/event.ts gains project.updated and comment.updated; project-service and comment-service emit them; activity-service records every event with the payload's occurredAt, resolves the project of a comment through the issue, adds the seven missing listeners, refuses a reversed range and walks every page by cursor (listAllActivity); activity-repository stores metadata and makes until inclusive; organization-service passes occurredAt; schemas/activity refines since <= until; the export route delegates to the service. Why hard: six symptom groups, each a different mechanism (listener wiring, event catalogue, write-time stamping, a shared repository predicate, a serialisation drop, a paging cap) — the obvious four reverts fix a third of the hidden cases; adding events versus direct record() calls must not double-write (hidden "exactly one entry per action"). Trap: the export must page by cursor, not by timestamp — every row of one fan-out shares an occurredAt, so a "move until down to the oldest row seen" walk (even with de-duplication) stops at 100 of 230 rows in the hidden bulk case, while a single-page export fails the same case.
